comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

All builtin textobject search is done with Lua patterns and certain false positives are to be expected (as [stated in docs](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/07ad48937204446ba350837a3413a5d19de22c36/doc/mini-ai.txt#L37-L38)).

Tags suffer the most from this. And nested tags is the most visible example. I couldn't find a reasonably not complicated approach to update [current Lua patterns](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/07ad48937204446ba350837a3413a5d19de22c36/lua/mini/ai.lua#L1094) to work in nested tags situation.

The main reason for the lack of trying to solve this is that I believe using some tree-sitter base approach is more appropriate here. The `tag` builtin was mostly added for completeness (with builtin textobject, 'targets.vim', and 'mini.surround') and expected to work in most basic situations.

#110 is relevant here.

labels.description: The behavior is not planned to be implemented
labels.name: not-planned
